The custom template is a Quarto website project with HTML reports and Reveal.js presentations.

## Get started

Quarto 1.8.25 or later is required. To download the starter template, run:

```{bash}
#| eval: false
#| filename: bash
quarto use template royfrancis/specky
```

The downloaded template does not include `_extensions/`. Install the required extensions before the first render:

```{bash}
#| eval: false
#| filename: bash
# adds Font Awesome icons
quarto add --no-prompt quarto-ext/fontawesome
# adds a two-logo header to slides
quarto add --no-prompt royfrancis/quarto-revealjs-header
# adds a presenter pointer to slides
quarto add --no-prompt royfrancis/quarto-revealjs-pointer
# adds collapsible code output
quarto add --no-prompt mcanouil/quarto-collapse-output@1.4.0
# adds Bootstrap accordion components
quarto add --no-prompt royfrancis/quarto-accordion
# adds Leaflet maps
quarto add --no-prompt royfrancis/quarto-leaflet
# adds team profile layouts
quarto add --no-prompt royfrancis/quarto-team
# adds Toast UI schedule components
quarto add --no-prompt royfrancis/quarto-toastui
```

The template command creates a website project that you can modify as needed. After installing the extensions, its key top-level files and directories are:

```
.
├── 404.md
├── assets/
├── _extensions/
├── home_about.qmd
├── home_coc.qmd
├── home_contents.qmd
├── home_faq.qmd
├── home_precourse.qmd
├── home_schedule.qmd
├── home_syllabus.qmd
├── index.qmd
├── schedule.csv
├── _metadata.yml
├── _quarto.yml
├── reports/
└── slides/
```

## Preview

Quarto provides a live preview while you edit.

```{bash}
#| eval: false
#| filename: bash
quarto preview
```

::: {.callout-warning}
Preview builds the entire project, so it may fail if any document is incomplete.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
The template sets `freeze: false` by default. Enabling [freeze](https://quarto.org/docs/projects/code-execution.html) stores computational output, which can speed up project renders and allow pages to render when the original computation environment or tools are unavailable.
:::

## Render

A Quarto document can be rendered from the terminal as follows:

```{bash}
#| eval: false
#| filename: bash

# render the full project (freeze works if enabled)
quarto render

# render a specific file (freeze is ignored for single-file renders)
quarto render reports/sample/index.qmd
```

This generates output in the `docs/` directory, as configured by `project: output-dir` in `_quarto.yml`. Global output defaults are defined under `format` in `_quarto.yml`; a document can override them in its YAML front matter. For example, `format: html` produces an HTML page, while `format: revealjs` produces a Reveal.js presentation.

## Settings

Start by updating `_quarto.yml`, which contains the project and website settings. See the documentation for [Quarto projects](https://quarto.org/docs/projects/quarto-projects.html) and [websites](https://quarto.org/docs/websites/).

- The output directory is set to **docs**; `output-dir: docs`
- Change `site-url` to your intended destination
- `open-graph: true` enables Open Graph metadata, and `website: image` sets the default image used in social link previews
- Navigation bar links are set under **website: navbar**. Add or remove as needed
- Page footer settings are set under **website: page-footer**. Check license. Update as needed
- HTML report settings are under **format: html:**
  - These are global defaults for all HTML pages and can be overridden in page front matter
  - A custom SCSS theme is defined (`assets/css/styles.scss`)
  - Table of contents is enabled (`toc: true`)
  - Sections are automatically numbered (`number-sections: true`)
  - Long code lines wrap instead of scrolling horizontally (`code-overflow: wrap`)
  - A default subtitle has been set
  - Last-modified dates are enabled by default (`date: last-modified`); the home pages override this with `date: ""`
  - A default listing image is set and can be overridden in page front matter (`image:`); a page-level override resolves relative to that document's own folder, not the project root, so reaching a project asset needs a depth-correct relative path such as `../../assets/images/example.webp`
  - Images can be clicked to open in a lightbox (`lightbox: auto`)
- Reveal.js presentation settings are under **format: revealjs**
  - These are global defaults for all Reveal.js presentations and can be overridden in page front matter
  - A custom SCSS theme is defined (`assets/css/slides.scss`)
  - All items on a slide appear at once (`incremental: false`), override with `.fragment` class
  - Use `##` to define slides (`slide-level: 2`)
  - Chalkboard for scribbling is enabled (`chalkboard: true`)
  - A custom image for each presentation can be set when viewing as listing (`image:`); the same folder-relative resolution described above for HTML reports applies
  - Set title slide graphic image (`hero:`)
  - Set title slide background image (`title-slide-attributes: data-background-image:`)
  - A default subtitle has been set
  - Adjust slide header logo image, size and link (`header-logo-*`); the `header-logo-*-url` values are used as-is with no automatic path resolution, so they must be written relative to where the presentation actually renders (`../../home_contents.html` for this template's fixed `slides/<name>/index.qmd` depth)
- `execute` settings
  - Executable code cells are evaluated (`eval: true`), and their source code is displayed (`echo: true`) by default
  - warnings and messages from chunks are disabled
  - `freeze: false` disables storage of computational output by default; set it to `true` or `auto` if needed
- Add any arbitrary metadata in `_metadata.yml` and use it across the project as `{{{< meta metadata >}}}`. This is used for map information.
- Custom filters and extensions
  - Extensions provide additional functionality
  - Filter extensions can be added globally in `_quarto.yml` or locally in individual qmd files
  - Add quarto version (`{{{< meta quarto_version >}}}`) or date/time (`{{{< meta current_year >}}}`), enabled through custom lua (`assets/custom.lua`)
  - Code output folding is enabled through the `quarto-collapse-output` extension. This is documented [here](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-collapse-output)
  - Font Awesome icons are enabled through the `fontawesome` extension. Use `{{{< fa icon-name >}}}` to insert an icon. See the [extension documentation](https://github.com/quarto-ext/fontawesome)
  - Accordions are enabled through the `quarto-accordion` extension. Define named accordion data under `accordion` in page front matter and render it with `{{{< accordion name >}}}`. See `home_faq.qmd` and the [extension documentation](https://github.com/royfrancis/quarto-accordion)
  - Leaflet maps are enabled through the `leaflet` extension. Add map information as metadata in `_metadata.yml` and use the shortcode `{{{< leaflet mapname >}}}` to include the map in any qmd file. Leaflet maps are documented [here](https://github.com/royfrancis/quarto-leaflet)
  - Team profiles are enabled through the `team` extension. Define profiles under `team` in page front matter and render a named group with `{{{< team name >}}}`. See `home_about.qmd` and the [extension documentation](https://github.com/royfrancis/quarto-team)
  - Toast UI schedules are enabled through the `toastui` extension. Define options under `toastui` in page front matter and render a named schedule with `{{{< toastui schedule >}}}`. In this template, `home_schedule.qmd` loads `schedule.csv`; each `calendarId` in the CSV must match an ID under `calendars`. See the [extension documentation](https://github.com/royfrancis/quarto-toastui)
  - Reveal.js [header with logos](https://github.com/royfrancis/quarto-revealjs-header) and [pointer](https://github.com/royfrancis/quarto-revealjs-pointer) extensions are enabled for slides. Press `q` on slides to show the pointer and `q` again to hide it
  - Remove an unused extension with `quarto remove <extension-id>`, for example, `quarto remove quarto-ext/fontawesome`
- Add document-specific CSS under `format: html: css` in page front matter if needed

## Content

You can now add course content.

{{< fa circle-info >}} The starter template should render completely using Quarto alone. Add R, Python or Julia code chunks as needed.

- The homepage is **index.qmd**
- Files named `home_*.qmd` are site pages. If you add, remove, or rename one, update `website: navbar` in `_quarto.yml` as needed
- **home_schedule.qmd** configures a Toast UI schedule that loads `schedule.csv`
- **home_contents.qmd** contains a Markdown table with links to reports and slides
- **home_about.qmd** contains organizer profiles and practical information such as venue and map details
- **home_faq.qmd** contains an accordion example with frequently asked questions
- **home_syllabus.qmd** shows tab panels
- **home_precourse.qmd** contains preparation instructions and a checklist
- **home_coc.qmd** contains the NBIS code of conduct
- Reports and slides are organized in separate folders under `reports/` and `slides/`, respectively
- `reports/index.qmd` and `slides/index.qmd` are listing pages that discover those documents

## Usage tips and conventions

- See Quarto's [Markdown basics](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/markdown-basics.html)
- Use level-2 headings (`##`) as the highest heading level
- Use Quarto-style chunk options, such as `#| eval: false`, rather than `` `{r eval=FALSE}` ``
- `.qmd` files beginning with `_`, such as `_content.qmd`, are child documents and are not rendered alone
- Include a child document with `{{{< include _content.qmd >}}}`. Includes do not work in `.ipynb` notebooks. [Includes are documented here](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/includes.html).
- Dynamic variables can be defined in `_variables.yml` and used as `{{{< var variable >}}}`. Dynamic variables are documented [here](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/variables.html).
- Custom metadata can be defined in `_metadata.yml` and used as `{{{< meta metadata >}}}`
- When using R or Python, declare all libraries in one chunk at the beginning of each document
- Add a session information chunk at the end of `.qmd` documents that use code. This helps with reproducibility and debugging. For R, use `sessionInfo()` or `sessioninfo::session_info()`. For Python, use `import session_info; session_info.show()`
